title: Pappardelle ai funghi misti
subtitle: Pappardelle with mixed wild mushrooms
excerpt: Wide egg pappardelle in a rich sauce of mixed wild mushrooms, cream, thyme, and Parmesan. A Tuscan autumn pasta: substantial, earthy, and deeply satisfying.
sourceNotes: Pappardelle with mushrooms is a classic of Tuscan autumn cooking, where wide pasta ribbons are matched with rich, robust sauces. Cross-referenced with Giuliano Bugialli, The Fine Art of Italian Cooking (1977).

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The mushroom sauce can be made a day ahead and reheated. Cook the pasta fresh.

content.text: Pappardelle ai funghi misti differs from tagliatelle ai funghi in one significant way: the cream. This is a cream-finished sauce rather than a clean butter-and-oil one, giving it more body and a richer, more autumnal character. Use whatever mix of mushrooms is available: porcini, chestnut, shiitake, or chanterelle. The rehydrated porcini are the flavour base; the fresh mushrooms give texture.

items.prepNote: pappardelle; or tagliatelle if pappardelle unavailable
or mixed fresh wild mushrooms, sliced
soaked in 150 ml hot water, liquid reserved
finely grated, plus more to serve

content.text: Soak the dried porcini in hot water for 20 minutes. Drain, reserving the soaking liquid. Chop roughly.
Bring a large pot of well-salted water to the boil for the pasta.

Heat the butter and olive oil in a wide frying pan over high heat. Add the fresh mushrooms and fry without stirring for 2 minutes. Toss and cook 3 minutes more until golden. Add the porcini and cook 1 minute.

Reduce heat to medium. Add the shallots and garlic and cook 3 minutes. Add the thyme. Pour in the wine and reduce by half. Add the porcini soaking liquid (leaving the last tablespoon behind) and simmer 3 minutes.
Pour in the cream. Simmer gently for 3 to 4 minutes until slightly thickened. Remove the thyme sprigs. Season.

Cook the {{pasta-dried}} until 1 minute short of packet time. Reserve a ladle of pasta water and drain. Add the pasta to the sauce. Toss over medium heat for 1 minute, adding pasta water if needed. Remove from heat, add Parmesan and parsley, toss, and serve.

items.cause: Too much pasta water or cream not reduced enough
items.fix: Reduce the sauce a little further before adding pasta. Add pasta water only a tablespoon at a time.

items.cause: Pan overcrowded or heat too low
items.fix: Fry mushrooms in batches over high heat. They must colour before releasing moisture.

items.cause: Heat too high when cream was added
items.fix: Add cream off the heat or over low heat and stir gently. If it splits, a splash of pasta water and vigorous stirring can bring it back.
Use only 100 ml cream and rely more on pasta water to loosen. Or omit cream for a cleaner version.

content.text: Pappardelle is a Tuscan pasta, wide and flat, suited to substantial, country sauces. Hare ragù (pappardelle al cinghiale or al lepre) is the classic pairing; mushroom cream sauce is the meatless equivalent, equally rich. In Tuscany in autumn, fresh porcini are gathered from the hills around Florence and Siena and brought to market the same morning. The quality of the mushrooms in this dish is the variable that matters most.
